- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.10) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns positive after a dip, model often fails to adjust forecast downward in the following 3–5 days.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes: model frequently forecasts a peak and then overcorrects downward, missing the true continuation or reversal.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices revert to historical mean too quickly, ignoring sentiment-driven momentum.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility; ignore short-term sentiment spikes for long-term trend alignment.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model tends to overcorrect downward — avoid aggressive downward revisions unless sentiment confirms bearish trend.
